source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Measurement
points: **Measurement** = comparing an unknown quantity with a fixed **standard unit**.
A measurement has two parts: a **number** and a **unit** (e.g. 5 metres).
Long ago people used **body parts** (handspan, cubit, foot, pace) — these varied from person to person, so **standard units** were needed.

sections.heading: 2. Units of Length
points: The **SI unit of length is the metre (m)**.
**1 metre = 100 centimetres (cm)**; **1 cm = 10 millimetres (mm)**; **1 kilometre (km) = 1000 m**.
Small lengths → mm/cm; large distances → km.

sections.heading: 3. Measuring Length Correctly
points: Use a suitable device: **ruler/scale, measuring tape**; for curved lengths use a thread.
Place the object **along the scale**; if the zero end is worn, start from another full mark and **subtract**.
Keep the **eye directly above** the reading point to avoid **parallax error** (wrong reading from a slanted view).

sections.heading: 4. Motion
points: **Motion** = a change in the **position** of an object with **time** (compared to a fixed point).
An object is **at rest** if its position does not change.
Motion and rest are **relative** — they depend on the reference point chosen.

sections.heading: 5. Types of Motion
points: **Rectilinear motion** — along a **straight line** (e.g. a car on a straight road, a marching soldier).
**Circular motion** — along a **circular path** (e.g. tip of a clock hand, a stone tied to a string and whirled).
**Rotational motion** — spinning about its own axis (e.g. a spinning top, a fan).
**Periodic / oscillatory motion** — repeating at regular intervals (e.g. a pendulum, a swing).
An object may show **more than one** type of motion at once (e.g. a moving bicycle wheel: rotational + rectilinear).

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Measurement = comparison with a standard unit; needs a number + a unit.
SI unit of length = metre; 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 km = 1000 m.
Parallax error = wrong reading from a slanted eye position; keep eye directly above.
Motion = change of position with time; rest & motion are relative.
Motion types: rectilinear (straight), circular, rotational (about axis), periodic/oscillatory.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **SI unit of length is the metre**, not the centimetre.
**Circular motion** (path is a circle) is different from **rotational motion** (spins about its own axis).
Rest and motion are **relative** to the chosen reference point.
If the scale's zero end is broken, **start from a full mark and subtract** — don't measure from the damaged end.
